message:
5 positional locator read(s) taken in the window an action opened, with no auto-retrying assertion between:
      card.spec.ts:40 — reads a positional locator written into the read itself in the window the action at line 39 opened: expect( await rimOf<' '>(page.locator(' ').first(), ' '), ).toBe(' ')
      card.spec.ts:48 — reads a positional locator written into the read itself in the window the action at line 47 opened: expect( await widthOf<' '>(page.locator(' ').nth(1), ' '), ).toBe(' ')
      card.spec.ts:56 — reads a positional locator written into the read itself in the window the action at line 55 opened: expect( await page .locator(' ') .last() .evaluate<string>((el) => getComputedStyle(el).bord
      card.spec.ts:67 — reads a positional locator written into the read itself in the window the action at line 66 opened: expect( await pick<Record<string, string>>(page.locator(' ').nth(2), {}), ).toBe(' ')
      card.spec.ts:75 — reads a positional locator written into the read itself in the window the action at line 74 opened: expect((await frameOf(page.locator(' ').last())).colour).toBe( ' ', )
    A
why: Five hovered or focused cards, each read through type syntax the scanner has to read past: `rimOf<'border-color'>(…)`, an arrow with type parameters; `pick<Record<string, string>>(…)`, whose type parameter and argument hold one of their own; `widthOf<'border-width'>(…)`, a function declaration with them; `frameOf`, a declaration whose type parameter holds one of its own and whose return annotation is `Promise<{ colour: string; width: string }>`; and Playwright's `evaluate<string>(…)`. A name followed by `<…>` and not by its `(` is no call to a pattern that wants the parenthesis next, a definition whose parameters come after its type parameters is no definition, and one whose annotation's `{` is taken for its body reads nothing — each read goes by unreported.
